changes: Fix loss of confirmed Tartarus instruments after a misread day. The observed 10 -> 18 -> 11 sequence incorrectly treated the lower day as a new run and dropped Executioner's Blacklist. A countdown regression no longer resets the run or confirmed instruments.

Unexpected day/length jumps are held pending a second consistent picture, with the existing bounded fresh-picture retries. Until verified, the last accepted board, tools, marks, vault and objective are preserved and no advice is issued for the suspect day. Normal same-day/next-day reads gain no fixed delay.

Fresh real Start events and initial offers reset a run explicitly. Duplicate/historical log starts do not erase a restored run. Manual instrument corrections made while a suspect picture is pending remain authoritative. Verification/epoch metadata does not change exact Monte Carlo cache keys.

Reproduced the reported 10 -> 18 -> 11 sequence in unit tests and the packaged overlay; verified forward/backward recovery, manual confirmation races, new-run reset/deduplication, bounded retry routing, full calculation budgets and rolling forecasts. Automatic updater from 1.0.3 remains unchanged; native solver and pixel-reader binaries are unchanged.

incident.cause: A misread countdown was treated as a new run; confirmed tools were discarded.

limitations: Update metadata and binaries are trusted through this GitHub repository over HTTPS and SHA256, not a separate Authenticode signing certificate.

Setup flags are verified with a harmless Windows probe and the real installer payload is extracted/compared/launched; tests do not install over the user application or modify registry installation state.

Portable replacement, backup cleanup, changed-staging recovery, Unicode/special paths and helper survival after host exit are tested on owned probe executables. Packaged update networking/UI uses only a loopback fake release; the fake update is not executed.
Checks/downloads are automatic; installation requires the user action and does not interrupt a run.
